version.change: [b]New![/b] Long press a transaction to select it, tap others to add them, then delete them together or move them to another wallet or category.
[b]New![/b] A debt card offers Pay in full and a credit card Receive in full, opening the editor on what is left, and every debt payment opens with the debt's description filled in.
[b]New![/b] The month row above the calendar day strip follows the strip as you scroll it, and tapping the marked month sends the strip to the first of that month.
[b]New![/b] A theme color shows on the screen while it is being picked, before OK.
The app draws behind the status and navigation bars on every Android version, and scrolling content stays reachable under them.
The calendar strip, the chart axes and the pie chart percentages write their numbers in the digits of the app's language.
The wallet name under the title on the calendar and on a category's transaction list is no longer cut off.
Deleting the open item on the wide two panel layout and then rotating no longer shows an empty panel full screen.
Nine currencies that stored no decimals now store two: AMD, CRC, ETB, GYD, MNT, MUR, RSD, TZS and UZS. Amounts already stored keep their value.
A settings row no longer loses its title after its color or the theme type changes in a dark theme.
A subcategory under a category kept out of the reports now says so, since none of its money reaches a report.
The Overview and the period screens update after a transaction is edited or deleted from inside them.
A budget no longer hides a transfer into a wallet that was removed from it.
[b]New![/b] Tap into the amount on the keypad to put a cursor there, then type or delete at that spot.
[b]New![/b] A period's transactions fold under their header on the transactions list, so a long list reads as a column of period totals.
External Memory can be set up as a backup destination on Android 13 and newer, where it never connected before.
Setting up a backup destination no longer closes the app.
Deleting a wallet, a transaction or a transfer no longer freezes the screen while it runs.
A restore that fails leaves your ledger exactly as it was, and an import that fails part way leaves nothing of it behind.
A row the app refuses during an import now stops the import and says so, where it used to be skipped in silence.
A budget save the app refused no longer closes the editor as if it had saved, an edited past period keeps its start day, and a budget takes its currency from its wallets.
A wallet in a currency this installation does not know stores a typed 12.50 as 12.50, where it stored 12.
The currency converter keeps updating while rates download.
A backup restored from another installation no longer leaves the app with no currency to offer.
Saving a budget, opening a wallet or the Overview no longer crashes on a currency the app cannot resolve.
An import can no longer lock up against a currency reload.
[b]New![/b] A home screen widget that shows one wallet's balance.
[b]New![/b] A budget can cover more than one category.
[b]New![/b] A category's total in the Overview opens into the subcategories it is made of.
[b]New![/b] 73 more category icons, filling the six picker groups that had none.
Back from a section you opened in the drawer returns to Transactions instead of closing the app.
The status bar follows the theme color on Android 15 and later, where it used to stay the window background.
A withdrawal dated before the deposit that funds it no longer takes a savings goal below zero.
A debt payment can no longer be filed against a wallet in another currency.
A savings goal or a debt stays in the currency its money is in.
A debt keeps the time of day on its own transaction.
The Overview and the screen it opens agree when a category is hidden from the reports.
[b]New![/b] A budget can repeat, opening its next period on its own when the one before it ends.
[b]New![/b] A transactions list says what came in and what went out over the period it is showing.
[b]New![/b] The calendar day strip marks the days that have transactions.
Opening a search result shows the transaction, where before it opened the editor.
The calendar keeps the day you picked, and shows which day that is when it is not today.
The calendar no longer lands on 1 January of the year before the one you asked for.
A detail panel survives a rotation on a screen wide enough to change how many panels fit.
Editing a debt's master transaction moves the debt with it.
A saving's deposit or withdraw no longer lets you move it to another wallet.
A saving refuses a withdraw larger than what the goal will hold, not just larger than what it holds today.
Restoring a backup opens the app on your ledger instead of the welcome screen.
Text is mirrored in a right to left layout in the places it was still left aligned.
Corrected the French wording shown after an import and in the two backup success messages.
[b]New![/b] Start a transaction from a person's screen with that person already attached.
Android's own backup stored nothing, so a restore brought back an empty app. It now carries the ledger.
Automatic backup says when a failure is what turned it off.
An income or expense color that would vanish into the page is drawn readable instead.
A debt's master transaction takes the debt's date, not the day it was typed.
A saving refuses a withdraw larger than it holds.
The child category arrow points at the child in a right to left layout.
CSV import reads a file that starts with a byte order mark.
[b]New![/b] Open a transaction and duplicate it.
[b]New![/b] Hide a category's child categories behind an arrow on its row.
The calculator divides correctly. 10 divided by 4 is 2.50.
The calculator will not hand back a negative amount, except for a wallet's Initial amount.
A Deposit or Withdraw on a saving opens with the wallet already filled in.
Save a transaction or transfer dated in the future and the app says the balance does not count it yet.
A list that looks empty now says when its rows are in other wallets or dated in the future.
A CSV import reads the whole file before writing any of it, so a bad row no longer leaves a half done import.
A CSV date with no time of day is accepted.
Transfers are left out of a CSV export, because a CSV cannot record them in a way the app can read back.
Deleting a transaction, a transfer or a wallet deletes the attachments that belonged to it, so they stop being carried in every backup.
A Local folder backup is written to the folder you picked, and a failed backup or restore no longer erases the folder and password you set.
[b]New![/b] Point the map at a tile server of your choosing.
[b]New![/b] Edit a recurrence after saving it.
[b]New![/b] Filter the debt lists down to the finished ones.
[b]New![/b] Tap a person to open their transactions.
A screen showing only one wallet names that wallet under its title.
Deleting the wallet you had selected no longer leaves every list empty. The app falls back to the total.
Automatic backup runs again, and no longer takes the app down at startup.
Automatic backup no longer keeps a notification on screen while it runs.
Calendar day and month labels no longer collapse to the same letters in several languages.
System category names follow the app language.
A transfer between currencies with different decimal counts keeps the rate you set.
[b]New![/b] Set the app language separately from the device, through Android's per app language setting.
In the dark themes the overview chart and the debt cards no longer show up white.
Percentages on the pie chart are centered and rounded correctly.
The Categories screen opens on Expenses.
The app no longer crashes on some language choices.
Debts paid off in full group with the finished ones and no longer inflate the amount still to pay.
Wallet notes are kept in backups.
Times follow the device 12 or 24 hour setting.
Recurring transfers open the right record.
[b]New![/b] Back up to your own WebDAV server, such as Nextcloud, ownCloud or a NAS, with no third party account and nothing sent to anyone else.
Build-system update for F-Droid binary transparency checks. No user-facing feature changes.
Build-system update to support F-Droid reproducible builds. No user-facing feature changes.
[b]New![/b] First Tallybook release, a maintained fork of MoneyWallet.
Tallybook is a separate app with its own application id and installs side by side with MoneyWallet.
Move your data across manually with backup and restore. See MIGRATION.md in the project for the verified steps.
Android 14 and 15 compatibility, including a fix for the startup crash on recent Android.
Import and export fixed under scoped storage.
Local folder backup option that works with file sync tools such as Syncthing.
Android 15 edge-to-edge UI polish so toolbars and controls are not covered by the system bars.
Original Tallybook launcher and welcome artwork.
